xray.one_line: A travel management company whose agents now search, book and service business trips from inside Claude, Google Chat and Teams, on the traveler's own credentials.
xray.what_it_does: American Express Global Business Travel (Amex GBT) describes itself as a software and services company for travel, expense, and meetings and events; its products include Egencia, Neo and Complete (built with SAP Concur), and it was taken private by Long Lake, which calls itself an AI holding company, in a $6.3 billion deal completed on 29 September 2026. Its stated AI strategy has three parts: revolutionise the customer experience, power the agentic transformation of B2B travel, and reduce operating costs. In July 2026 it launched an agent-to-agent (A2A) layer that routes traveler requests to specialised agents, with the Egencia AI connector in Claude as its first deployment. [s9, s1, s3, s11, s12, s10, s2]

situations.title: Booking business trips from Claude
reach: The traveler's calendar for the coming month
The traveler's credentials: Claude acts on the traveler's behalf
End-to-end air and hotel bookings: transactions, not only retrieval
Company configured policies, traveler profiles and corporate agreements
Amex GBT marketplace inventory of airlines and hotels
Transaction data fed into reporting systems
asked_our_example: Read calendar entries that imply business travel, to propose trips.
Book air and hotel only within the company's configured policy, and only trips the traveler has confirmed.
No changes to the traveler's profile or account settings.
gap: The connector acts with the traveler's credentials, so what it can do is whatever the traveler can do, while the request was only to help book confirmed trips.
Calendar access is the whole calendar, while the task needs only the entries that imply travel.

situations.title: Servicing chat with handoff to counselors
reach: Help-centre content the virtual agent is trained on
Traveler account actions: password resets, adding frequent flyer numbers
Live travel counselors who join or take over the conversation
Changing booked travel through Egencia AI
asked_our_example: Answer common questions from help-centre content.
Account self-service and invoice lookup only for the signed-in traveler.
Changes to booked travel go to a counselor or are confirmed by the traveler.
gap: Account changes and invoice retrieval happen in chat; how the agent ties each request to the signed-in traveler is not publicly documented.
Egencia AI can change travel, so a servicing chat reaches money as well as answers.

situations.title: Hotel sourcing with Hotel Lobby
reach: Client hotel sourcing data, cleansed by the agents
Negotiated-rate benchmarks across thousands of properties and supplier performance from more than $5 billion of managed hotel spend
Compliance trends across Amex GBT's client portfolio
Wish (target) rates that set the negotiating position
RFPs to hotels, validated by the agents
asked_our_example: Prepare and validate one client's sourcing data and RFPs.
Consultants keep responsibility for strategy, negotiations and exceptions (publicly stated).
gap: Agents working for one client draw on benchmarks and compliance trends from across Amex GBT's whole client portfolio.
Wish rates the agents calculate set the starting point of a negotiation the consultant owns.

questions: When the Egencia AI connector acts with a traveler's credentials, what can those credentials reach beyond booking, and can a company restrict the connector to search only or require a confirm step before purchase?
In the A2A layer, is there a record per action of which specialised agent did what, on whose authority, that a customer can export for audit?
How does the chat agent tie a password reset, loyalty change or invoice request to the signed-in traveler?
In Hotel Lobby, how is benchmark and compliance data from other clients separated from the client being sourced?
Under Long Lake, will client travel data be used to improve the Nexus platform shared across Long Lake companies?

It is read-only: never in the request path.
